output.title: Retrieval quality is a workflow constraint, not a nice-to-have
output.body:
If your AI tool has to look up information to do useful work, retrieval quality is part of the workflow design. Not a nice-to-have. When the system searches documents, emails, FAQs, or prior records, it needs to pull back the right material consistently, or the answer can look polished and still be wrong. That means rework for you, or a confident mistake for everyone else.

For a small business owner, the useful question is not “can AI answer this?” It is “can it find the right source every time this task runs?” If one recurring task makes you search more than one place for the answer, retrieval has become a design constraint. That could be customer questions, invoice checks, or lead follow-up.

The practical next step is simple: pick one recurring workflow and audit the source material behind it. Are the documents named clearly, grouped sensibly, and kept current? If the inputs are messy, automation usually moves the manual work earlier instead of removing it.

Bareni’s self-built local knowledge-assistant demo shows grounded answers with sources on synthetic data, but the public route is locked, so treat that as a demo pattern, not a deployed service. As a rule of thumb, if you would not trust a person to answer from a pile of badly labelled files, do not ask a system to do it quietly.
